title: Announcing the uqulang 0.1 preview
body: Blog 0.1 preview 26 September 2026 {{hijri:2026-09-26}} Release Announcing the uqulang 0.1 preview The compiler is self-hosting, the toolchain is one binary, and both are now shipping to universities. This is a preview, and the version number is doing honest work. uqulang began with a narrow complaint: writing systems code still means choosing between a language that tells you exactly what the machine will do and a language you can comfortably read. C gives you the first. Swift gives you the second. Most of the time you pick one and pay for the other for years. 0.1 is the first version where t

title: What works today
body: A self-hosting compiler producing native binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows on x86-64 and aarch64. Structs, enums with payloads, exhaustive pattern matching, traits, generics with static dispatch. Optionals, typed throws , defer , scope-based ownership with move . C interop in both directions at the ABI level, with no bindings generator. uqu build / run / test / fmt / check / doc / lsp in one b

title: What is deliberately missing
body: A preview that pretends to be complete wastes everybody's time. These are known gaps, not oversights: No dependency manager. Dependencies are paths and archives for now. The design is being written. No concurrency story. Threads exist through the C library; structured concurrency is designed and unshipped. Generics are incomplete. Generics over constant values — the thing fixed-capacity containers

title: On benchmarks
body: New languages usually launch with a graph. We are not going to, yet. The generated code is already close to what clang emits at -O2 for the loops we have measured, but “close on our machines, on our examples” is not a claim worth publishing. 0.2 ships a benchmark harness to licensed institutions — hardware description, compiler flags, input data and raw timings — and the numbers will be whatever t

title: Where feedback helps most
body: Not all feedback is equally useful at this stage. In rough order: Diagnostics that were unhelpful. If the compiler was right but the message did not tell you what to change, that is a bug worth filing. Ownership friction. Real code where the ownership rules forced an awkward structure. These cases shape 0.2. C interop gaps. A header the compiler cannot express, a layout mismatch, a calling convent

title: A note on where this comes from
body: uqulang is designed and built in Saudi Arabia. The name comes from عقل — ʿaql , the reasoning mind — and the mark is drawn from its first letter. Both the language and the documentation are developed in English and Arabic, because the people who will use it read both. Install it, break it, and tell us where it bent: installation guide · request a licence · support portal . Back to All posts Next I

title: uqu run
body: Everything after -- goes to your program, not to the compiler. Copy

title: uqu test
body: Copy --filter <text> Run only tests whose name contains the text. --fail-fast Stop at the first failure. --jobs <n> Run tests in parallel; 1 makes ordering deterministic. --format <kind> pretty (default) or json for CI ingestion.

title: uqu fmt
body: One style, no options, so formatting never becomes a review topic. Use --check in CI to fail on unformatted code. Copy

title: Exit codes
body: Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Compilation error, test failure, or unformatted code under --check 2 Bad usage: unknown flag, missing argument 101 Internal compiler error — please report it with the source that triggered it

title: Environment
body: UQU_HOME Toolchain directory. Defaults to ~/.uqulang . UQU_CACHE Build cache location. Delete it freely; it only costs time. UQU_TARGET Default target triple, overridden by --target . NO_COLOR Any value disables coloured diagnostics.

title: 1. Install the toolchain
body: If you have not installed uqu yet, follow the installation guide — it is one command on every supported platform. Then confirm the compiler can see everything it needs: Copy

title: 2. Create a project
body: uqu init writes the smallest project that builds: a manifest, a source directory and one module. Copy The manifest is deliberately small. There is no build script: uqu.toml Copy

title: 3. Write and run a program
body: Open src/main.uqu . Every executable needs exactly one main , and main may declare that it throws. src/main.uqu Copy Build and run it in one step: Copy Source files are UTF-8, and string literals hold arbitrary Unicode. Identifiers are ASCII in 0.1; wider identifier support is planned .

title: 4. Add a type
body: Structs hold data with a layout you can predict — fields in declaration order, C-compatible padding rules. Behaviour is attached with impl , not inheritance. src/greeting.uqu Copy Import it from main by module path: src/main.uqu Copy

title: 5. Handle a failure
body: Anything that can fail says so in its signature. The caller must respond — with try to propagate, or match to handle. src/main.uqu Copy If the file is missing, the error reaches main , the process exits non-zero, and the message goes to stderr — no stack unwinding, no silent default: Copy

title: 6. Write a test
body: Tests live next to the code they test, in the same file or a sibling one. The runner is built in; there is nothing to add to the manifest. src/greeting.uqu Copy Copy

title: 7. Build for release
body: A release build turns on optimisation and strips debug information. The result is a single static binary you can copy to any machine with the same target triple. Copy

title: What uqulang is
body: uqulang is a statically typed, ahead-of-time compiled language for systems work: operating system components, embedded firmware, codecs, databases, game engines, and the layer underneath applications. It produces native binaries with no runtime and no garbage collector, and it interoperates with C at the ABI level rather than through a binding layer. It is licensed to universities and research ins

title: What uqulang is not
body: Not a scripting language. There is no REPL-first workflow and no dynamic typing. Everything is checked before it runs. Not a borrow checker. Lifetimes are scope-based and explicit. The compiler catches use-after-move and double-free, but it does not attempt to prove every aliasing property. Not finished. 0.1 is a preview. Generics over constant values, async I/O and the package registry are design

title: Stability and versioning
body: Until 1.0, the language may change in a breaking way in any minor release. Each release ships a written migration note, and uqu fix applies the mechanical parts of a migration to your source. If you have written C, C++, Swift, Rust or Go, you can read this in one sitting. Covers toolchain 0.1.0 · updated {{build_date}} Bindings let binds a value that cannot be reassigned; var binds one that can. Types are inferred from the initialiser, and written explicitly when you want the contract visible. Copy There is no uninitialised binding. title: Bindings
body: let binds a value that cannot be reassigned; var binds one that can. Types are inferred from the initialiser, and written explicitly when you want the contract visible. Copy There is no uninitialised binding. A declaration without a value must be assigned on every path before it is read, and the compiler checks that.

title: Numbers and operators
body: Integer types name their width: i8 … i64 , u8 … u64 , plus isize and usize for pointer-sized values. There are no implicit conversions between them — a widening conversion is still written down. Copy

title: Control flow
body: if , while and for behave as you expect. Conditions are bool ; an integer is not a condition. guard states a precondition and must exit the scope. Copy

title: Functions
body: Parameters are immutable bindings. Pass a pointer when the callee must write through it, and the call site shows it with & . Copy

title: Structs
body: A struct is data with a predictable layout: fields in declaration order, alignment following the platform C rules. Methods live in an impl block, and self is explicit. Copy @layout("c") pins a struct to the exact C layout when you need to share it across an FFI boundary.

title: Enums and pattern matching
body: Enums carry payloads, and match must cover every case. An uncovered case is a compile error, not a warning — which is what makes adding a variant safe. Copy Patterns also match values, ranges and tuples: Copy

title: Optionals
body: ?T is a value that may be absent. There is no null pointer hiding inside an ordinary type, and an optional must be unwrapped before use. Copy

title: Errors
body: A function that can fail is marked throws , optionally with the error type it throws. Callers propagate with try or handle with match . Errors are ordinary values moving up the call stack — there is no unwinding machinery and no cost when nothing fails. Copy Ignoring a failure is possible, but you have to write it: discard try f() . Grep finds every one of them.

title: Memory and ownership
body: Values live on the stack. Heap allocation is a function call you can see, and every allocation has exactly one owner. When the owner goes out of scope, the memory is released — no collector, no reference counting unless you opt into it. Copy defer runs at scope exit, in reverse order of declaration. move transfers ownership; the source binding is dead afterwards. Reading a moved-from binding is a

title: Arrays, slices and strings
body: [N]T is a fixed-size array. []T is a slice: a pointer and a length, bounds-checked in debug builds. str is a UTF-8 slice of bytes with no terminator. Copy

title: Traits and generics
body: A trait is a set of requirements a type can satisfy. Generic functions are monomorphised — one specialised copy per concrete type, dispatched statically, with no vtable unless you ask for dynamic dispatch with dyn . Copy

title: Modules and visibility
body: One file is one module, named by its path from the source root. Nothing leaves a module unless it is marked pub , and there are no header files to keep in sync. Copy Copy

title: C interoperability
body: Declaring a C function is enough to call it: no bindings generator, no marshalling, no wrapper library. The call is a direct call with the platform ABI. Copy And in the other direction — exporting for C to call: Copy

title: Attributes
body: @inline / @noinline Force or forbid inlining of a function. @layout("c") Use the platform C layout and padding for a struct. @export("name") Expose a symbol under an exact name for C callers. @deprecated("use x") Warn at every use site, with your message. @target(os: "linux") Compile a declaration only for matching targets.

title: Tests
body: test blocks are part of the language, not a library. They are compiled out of release builds entirely. Copy

title: Planned, not yet shipped
body: These are designed and discussed, and not in 0.1. Do not write code against them yet. Generics over constant values, for fixed-capacity containers. Compile-time evaluation beyond constant folding. Structured concurrency and non-blocking I/O in the standard library. A package registry and a lockfile format. body: The script downloads the build for your platform, verifies its SHA-256 checksum against the signed manifest, unpacks it into ~/.uqulang and registers your licence key. Nothing is written outside your home directory and nothing needs sudo . macOS Linux Windows macOS macOS 13 or newer, on Apple silicon or Intel. title: Verify the install
body: Every release publishes a SHA256SUMS file and a detached signature. Verifying takes ten seconds and is worth doing on any machine you care about: Copy uqu doctor is the first thing to run when something looks wrong, and the first thing to paste into a bug report.

title: Lab and offline deployment
body: A teaching lab usually cannot run an installer per machine, and often has no outbound internet at all. Both cases are supported by the same archive. Download the platform archive once from the licence portal , put it on your image or file share, and point machines at it. Nothing about the evaluation build is cut down — it is the shipping compiler. Run a pilot for one semester before committing to a campus licence. title: Asking for changes
body: Licensed institutions shape the language. Feature requests go through your named contact, are answered in writing, and the accepted ones appear on the roadmap above with the release they are scheduled for. Requests that come from a course that is actually running carry the most weight — teaching friction is the most useful signal we get.

title: Using the name and mark
body: The name “uqulang” and the mark may be used in course descriptions, syllabi, lecture material, academic papers and talks, and to say that software was written in uqulang. They may not be used as the name of another product, or in a way that implies a partnership that does not exist.
